newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE March white sugar claws back over support.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE March white sugar claws back over support.

text.p: London's March white sugar contract dipped briefly below $300 late in Friday's session but steady buying ensured that the psychological support level remained relatively intact, traders said.
All contracts were trapped in tight ranges of around $2 and the two nearby spreads stayed mostly flat throughout the day.

Early commission house selling of March/May kept the spot value under pressure but the weakness was countered by mixed light buying and also the slight firmness in the New York market. The white premium was reasonably steady at around $67.
At 1642 GMT March was down 30 cents at $301.30 and May down 10 cents at $301.00. Volume amounted to 1,622 lots, boosted by some against actuals trades.
Technical analysts said nearby resistance for March should come from the convergence of three short-term moving averages around $303.50.
If the start of a bull run were to be confirmed then March would have to move above $312.80, the high scored on January 6, they said.

But this would entail breaking further resistance levels at $305, $308 and $310. Results have yet to emerge from Libya's buying tender and European sugar traders said it was still unclear whether anything had been bought at all or if Libya had passed on the offers received or postponed the tender.
Paris futures were slightly lower in thin trade.
March was down 70 cents at $300.80 and May down 20 cents at $301.00. Matif volume was 226 lots.
